grantAnyone: Letting anyone use your agents needs your vault passphrase.

platforms.slack: DM the bot or mention it in a channel — it answers in the thread. No public address needed.
platforms.telegram: Chat with your agents from your phone, in private or in groups. Set up in a minute with @BotFather.
platforms.teams: Bring agents into chats and channels through an Azure bot. Needs a public https address.

person.youTitle: Your agents' questions come here, and your replies answer them

connect.title: Connect {{platform}}
connect.description: Talk to your agents right where you already chat.
connect.agentsHint: Chats start with the first one; people switch with {{command}}.

telegram.step1: Open @BotFather, Telegram's bot for making bots.
telegram.step2: Send /newbot, then pick a display name and a username that ends in bot.
telegram.step3: BotFather answers with a token like 123456789:AAE… — copy it for the next step.

slack.step1: Create the app from Godmode's manifest — it brings the permissions, Socket Mode and the {{command}} command. Pick your workspace and confirm.
slack.step2: Install App → Install to your workspace, then copy the Bot User OAuth Token (xoxb-…).
slack.step3: Basic Information → App-Level Tokens → Generate a token with the connections:write scope and copy it (xapp-…).
slack.socketNote: Socket Mode keeps the connection outgoing: Slack never needs to reach this computer.

teams.step1: In the Azure portal, create an Azure Bot with type Single Tenant. Note its Microsoft App ID and your tenant ID.
teams.step2: Configuration → Manage Password → New client secret, and copy its Value.
teams.step4: Teams delivers messages over https, so Godmode needs a public address — a tunnel like cloudflared or ngrok pointing at {{host}}, or a server. You'll get the messaging endpoint for Azure after connecting.
teams.step4Cloud: Teams delivers messages over https, so Godmode needs a public address — a tunnel like cloudflared or ngrok pointing at Godmode on that computer, or a server. You'll get the messaging endpoint for Azure after connecting.

connect.liveApproved: Send it a message. The first time, you approve yourself here — that's how strangers stay out.
connect.liveAnyone: Send it a message — your agents answer right there.
connect.slackInvite: In channels, invite it with /invite @{{name}} and mention it.
